registered_note: Registered before any E3 batch result; revision 2 (three-type classification) replaces the whole-motion primary family of revision 1 (commit fdd5724) before the batch started. Development data: one E2 run (p0_W0g_task9_seed28_d1) used to debug and time the pipeline and to look at its frame-level split into reachable and unreachable frames; the sensitivity analysis repeats the primary family without it. Pipeline check started before the batch: reproduction of the FBLS release jogging example (author kinematics, ground reactions and static-optimization results) with the E3 static optimization and joint reactions; its outcome is reported with E3 and decides whether the lumbar part is interpreted
question: Where an output-layer root correction (E1 W0X, E2 W0g) changes an upper-body ergonomic assessment of the generated motion, is the change (1) a distortion made by our conversion into the models, (2) motion the human body cannot produce, or (3) producible motion that carries a higher load

type1_conversion.meaning: The models do not reproduce the generated skeleton, or a convention of the evaluation (axes, clamps, joint frames) misreads it. A property of the evaluation, not of the motion
type1_conversion.run_flags: Persistent fit error: run median of the per-frame IK marker RMS > 0.03 m (lumbar) or run median C2/skull fit error > 2 deg, chest fit > 1 deg, T1 fit > 5 mm (neck); a coordinate held at a non-anatomical model limit; joint-reaction finite on < 95% of frames
type1_conversion.gate: Type-1 rate per arm reported first. If it exceeds 5% in any control arm (C0, G0, G4) the conversion is treated as faulty and types 2 and 3 are not interpreted until it is fixed. Type-1 runs are excluded pairwise from types 2 and 3
type1_conversion.known_and_fixed: pelvis heading clamp at +-90 deg (E1Y/E2Y; FBLS pelvis and HYOID base unclamped); FBLS vertebral frames aligned with ground in the neutral pose, so compression is resolved along the spine tangent from model geometry (L5-S1 18.7 deg forward of the L5 frame y-axis); muscle-model conversion of FBLS rejected (passive forces)

type2_unreachable.meaning: Converted correctly, but the motion asks for forces the body cannot produce or postures it cannot reach

frame_flags.external: whole-body residual force > 5% BW (the E1 unsupported criterion)
frame_flags.lumbar_internal: any lumbar reserve torque > 1 N m
frame_flags.neck_internal: any neck reserve torque > 1 N m
frame_flags.kinematic: a lumbar or neck coordinate within 0.5 deg of its anatomical range limit

type2_unreachable.outcome: Fraction of trimmed frames flagged, per region (lumbar region: external, lumbar_internal or lumbar kinematic; neck region: neck_internal or neck kinematic)

type3_loaded.meaning: Reachable motion whose load or posture carries injury risk
type3_loaded.frames: Per region, the trimmed frames of a type-1-free run not flagged as type 2 for that region
type3_loaded.outcomes: L5-S1 compression along the spine tangent (95th percentile and mean, BW) and fraction of frames above the NIOSH 3400 N action limit; L5-S1 anterior-posterior shear (95th percentile) against 700 / 1000 N (Gallagher & Marras 2012); C7-T1 compression (95th percentile, BW); shoulder resultant moment; posture: ISO 11226 zone fractions over all type-1-free frames

interpretation: Type-2 increases mean that the correction makes the motion physically impossible in that region; their loads are not ergonomic risk, and joint reactions on those frames (reserves carry the excess) are not analysed. Type-3 differences are ergonomic differences of producible motion. Absolute load levels are model-dependent; paired differences within one model are interpreted, and absolute levels are only compared with the published range
data: Every run evaluated by E1 (config/e1_biomech_20261101.json, 1080 M2 runs) and E2 (config/e2_biomech_20261102.json, 576 P0 runs); generated motions read only, no new generation

pipeline.worker: python/scripts/run_e3_upper.py (module utils/motiogen/upper_body.py, OpenSim 4.6); biomech.py unchanged; per-frame series kept on the data disk for the frame classification
pipeline.posture: From the generated joint rotations: trunk relative to pelvis and neck relative to chest as Z-X-Y angles, trunk and head inclination from vertical, upper-arm elevation relative to the chest, head angular speed
pipeline.lumbar: FBLS full-body lumbar spine model (Raabe & Chaudhari 2016, 324 Thelen muscles) with the E1 pipeline: per-segment scaling to 75 kg, joint-centre IK with axial spine markers (weight 0.3) registered in a lumbar-locked first second, pelvis coordinates unclamped, 6 Hz filter, contact-constrained ground reactions, inverse dynamics, static optimization (activation squared, reserves 1000 pelvis / 1 lumbar and legs / 200 arms), joint reactions at L5-S1 ... L1-L2 from the static-optimization forces; shoulder resultant moment from the FBLS inverse dynamics
pipeline.neck: HYOID head-neck model (Mortensen et al. 2018, 72 Millard muscles, rigid tendon) with the impact actuators removed, head-neck masses scaled by 75/79.54 kg, the 6-DOF base driven by the generated chest; per-frame least-squares fit of the six independent neck coordinates to the generated neck and head rotations relative to the chest (T1 at the generated neck joint); inverse dynamics, static optimization (reserves 1e4 base / 1 N m neck), joint reactions at C7-T1 and C0-C1 driven by the static-optimization controls

primary.family: Eight hypotheses, Holm-adjusted at 0.05 over the exact sign-flip p values

contrasts.e1: W0X - C0, pooled over offsets 0.1/0.5/1.0 m
contrasts.e2: W0g - G4, pooled over offsets 0.5/1.0 m

hypotheses.type2_lumbar: type-2 frame fraction of the lumbar region; directional (> 0): supported when Holm p < 0.05 and the lower 95% bound > 0
hypotheses.type2_neck: type-2 frame fraction of the neck region; directional (> 0), as above
hypotheses.type3_lumbar: L5-S1 tangent compression 95th percentile on reachable frames (BW); two-sided: a difference when Holm p < 0.05 and the interval excludes 0
hypotheses.type3_neck: C7-T1 compression 95th percentile on reachable frames (BW); two-sided, as above

primary.pooling: One difference per task-seed-offset, equal-weight task means, cluster t interval (G = 24, G - 1 df), exact sign-flip p; type-3 statistics per run over its own reachable frames

secondary: type-1 rate by arm and flag (reported first, gate above)
type-2 split by flag (external, internal, kinematic) and its timing relative to the correction windows
type-3 sensitivity on frames reachable in both runs of a pair (time-matched)
type-3: L4-L5 and L1-L2 compression, L5-S1 shear against 700 / 1000 N, NIOSH fraction, shoulder moment, trunk and neck muscle-group activations, C0-C1 compression
posture: ISO 11226 zone fractions and posture endpoints
E1: W0 - C0, XFh - C0, XFo - C0, W0X - W0; E2: G4 - G0, G4W - G4, W0g - G0 on every primary outcome
absolute type-3 levels of the control arms against the published walking range (L5-S1 / L4-L5 peak compression about 0.9-2.6 BW for walking; FBLS static-optimization studies report up to 3.8 BW)
sensitivity of the primary family without the development run
conventions_not_derived: Type-1 gate 5%; type-2 thresholds 1 N m reserve and 0.5 deg from range limits; residual 5% BW as E1
Static optimization at 10 Hz for FBLS (about 4 s per frame for 324 muscles) and 50 Hz for HYOID
Spine tangent from adjacent intervertebral joint centres as the compression axis

Joint reactions of FBLS from the static-optimization forces file; of HYOID from the static-optimization controls with rigid-tendon muscles (the forces-file override returned NaN on most HYOID frames; converting FBLS to Millard muscles added passive forces of several hundred N per hip flexor)
Axial spine marker weight 0.3; HYOID mass scaling by body-mass ratio; ISO 11226 static zones applied frame by frame to dynamic motion
estimated_hours: about 42 with 14 OpenSim workers (development run: neck 3 min, lumbar 18 min per run); the 720 primary-arm runs first, about 18
